text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of chorioamnionitis, low Apgar scores, and early-onset seizures, early-onset neonatal sepsis is highly suspected. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture, CSF_Analysis, CBC.

text: Given the maternal history of chorioamnionitis and the neonate's early-onset seizures, I suspect Group B Streptococcus or E. coli meningitis. REQUEST TEST: CSF_Gram_Stain, CSF_Culture, Blood_Glucose.

text: The normal blood glucose rules out hypoglycemia, so we must focus on infectious meningitis given the chorioamnionitis history. REQUEST TEST: CSF_Glucose, CSF_Protein, CSF_Cell_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: The CSF findings of low glucose, elevated protein, and elevated cell count strongly confirm bacterial meningitis. I will now initiate empiric antibiotic therapy and request imaging to assess for complications. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of early-onset seizures, lethargy, and ill appearance in a preterm infant with a history of chorioamnionitis is classic for early-onset neonatal sepsis and meningitis. The CSF findings of low glucose, elevated protein, and elevated cell count confirm bacterial meningitis. Given the prematurity and chorioamnionitis, Group B Streptococcus is the most likely pathogen. DIAGNOSIS READY: Group B Streptococcus Meningitis
